conclusion_detail.narrative:
The run supported both explanations: NVDA’s margin advantage over AAPL and MSFT reflected a durable difference in profitability, and it was also explained by faster revenue growth over the same periods. Overall, the evidence pointed strongly in both directions rather than choosing one over the other.

Both claims were supported, each with high confidence and no refuting evidence. The first claim held that NVDA’s net margin advantage was a durable difference across the same periods. The second claim also held that the advantage was explained by faster revenue growth over the same periods.

The loop ran a correlation analysis, then a simple regression, then another correlation analysis, and it stopped because it had sufficient evidence. What remains open is whether the margin gap stays persistent across periods or narrows or reverses over time, and whether controlling for revenue growth removes most of the observed margin advantage.
